title: EventStream hiccup — repro notes and quick triage
content:
Quick brain dump and exact repro attempts for the intermittent event-stream hiccup we saw in canary yesterday. Goal: capture commands, observed outputs, and immediate hypotheses so anyone can pick this up and run repros without digging through logs.

Symptom summary:
- Clients (hosted-api Node / browser) sometimes see the stream stall for 300–800ms between small chunks, then resume. Not a full disconnect — stream resumes with next chunk.
- Observed across HTTP/1.1 SSE and HTTP/2 streaming endpoints. More common when request QPS is > 150/s on a single host.
- No consistent 5xx, mostly long pauses then normal steady stream.

What I tried (exact commands + results)
1) curl (baseline, HTTP/1.1 SSE) - Command: curl --no-buffer -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-lite" - Result: saw repeated "data: ...\n\n" chunks. On pause reproduce: timestamps below show ~600ms gap. curl prints nothing special.

2) node fetch streaming (client-ish) - test-client.js (snippet):
const res = await fetch(url);
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  console.log(`got ${value.length} bytes`);
}
- Observed: logs: got 24 bytes, got 0 bytes (stall), [600ms], got 18 bytes. No thrown error.

3) curl with http2 enabled - Command: curl --http2 -v --no-buffer "https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-lite" - Result: same behavior. On the wire saw SETTINGS frames earlier, but no RST_STREAM.

4) python aiohttp client (concurrent) - Script: uses aiohttp.ClientSession().get(...).content.iter_chunked(128) - Observed: similar stalls, sometimes exception: ClientPayloadError: Response payload is not completed

5) reproducer server (local) to mimic our runtime write pattern - Node server that writes many small chunks with setTimeout((), 20) between writes. Reproduces stalls locally only when server behind an nginx reverse proxy with proxy_buffering on. Disabling proxy buffering removed stalls.

Server-side logs from canary host (snips):
Mar 11 14:22:08 host-12 rtd-infer[pid]: wrote chunk-size=24 seq=97 elapsed=14ms
Mar 11 14:22:08 host-12 rtd-infer[pid]: flush-wait=620ms seq=98 wrote=18
Mar 11 14:22:09 host-12 envoy[pid]: [warning] http2 stream window exceeded, reducing write immediacy

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Envoy / proxy flow-control interaction on HTTP/2 causes bursts to be coalesced or delayed when the peer window is exhausted — we see a warning line.
2) Intermediate buffering (nginx/proxy) plus Nagle/socket coalescing delays small writes until buffer thresholds/timeouts.
3) Server batching logic (continuous batching) flush heuristic is too conservative under high small-chunk QPS.
4) Client-side read scheduling in certain runtimes (node/v8 timer clumping) amplifies perceived pauses.

Immediate next steps to validate: list of reproducible experiments
- Repro A: run canary host with envoy log-level debug on http2, capture detailed SETTINGS/WINDOW updates. (I can run this on host-12) - Command to toggle: sudo systemctl set-environment ENVOY_LOG_LEVEL=debug && systemctl restart envoy
- Repro B: run the same Node micro-reproducer behind our local envoy (config copied from canary) and vary SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE to large (1MB) vs small (64KB) - Go client: use net/http with TransportForceAttemptHTTP2 bool set and log flow control windows.
- Repro C: toggle proxy_buffering in nginx (if used) or envoy tcp_proxy

Notes from quick experiments:
- Disabling Nagle (SO_NODELAY) on the server socket reduced median pause from ~420ms to ~80ms in local tests.
- Increasing HTTP/2 initial window size removed the pause in our local envoy reproducer (strong signal).

Possible mitigations (short-term):
- Increase SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE in envoy for streaming endpoints. Risk: memory increase per stream.
- Aggressively coalesce small writes at the runtime to reduce pressure (send 256B chunks instead of 24B).
- Add per-route config to bypass proxy buffering or tune flow-control for realtime routes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which layer is the dominant contributor on real canary: envoy or runtime? (I suspect combo).
- Can we add a tracing span at write->tcp-flush to measure kernel buffer latency? (Benji suggested eBPF quick trace).
- Need to check client-side browser impact vs node. Reports from mobile clients? (ask CS)

Immediate asks for reviewers:
- Aisha: can you run the envoy window-size test on canary host-12 (I gave commands in repro B)?
- Benji: can you try toggling SO_NODELAY in the runtime container and paste microbench results?

Links and artifacts:
- Linear: RED-4321 (streaming hiccups, customer report)
- Slack thread pinned in linked_artifacts above

If you pick this up: start with the envoy window-size experiment (most likely cause), capture pcap + envoy debug logs, and ping me. I'll hold off changing default configs until we have memory/cost tradeoffs.

Scratchpad end — EM
